requirements.requirement: Carry two tagged VLANs (10, 20) over the shared physical link connecting node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: node1 eth1 was configured with 8021q sub-interfaces eth1.10 (vid10) and eth1.20 (vid20) carrying the two VLANs over the shared link, confirmed up with correct IPs. node2 and node3 each added a matching vlan10/vlan20 sub-interface bound to enp8s0, the same shared NIC on the trunk network, confirmed via ip addr output.

requirements.requirement: node2 placed in VLAN10 in its own subnet with node1 as router, and can reach node1
requirements.summary: node2 vlan10 sub-interface configured with 10.10.10.2/24; ping to node1's 10.10.10.1 gateway succeeded (0% loss).

requirements.requirement: node3 placed in VLAN20 in its own subnet with node1 as router, and can reach node1
requirements.summary: node3 vlan20 sub-interface configured with 10.10.20.2/24; ping to node1's 10.10.20.1 gateway succeeded (0% loss).

requirements.requirement: Traffic between node2 and node3 (different VLANs) is refused, while each still reaches node1 on its own VLAN
requirements.summary: Direct cross-VLAN pings failed by default (no route, Destination Host Unreachable) in both directions. To rule out this being merely a missing-route artifact, the executor added a temporary route on node2 toward node3's subnet via node1 and re-pinged; node1 actively rejected the forwarded traffic (Destination Port Unreachable from firewall REJECT), directly demonstrating enforced isolation rather than incidental unreachability. The temporary test route was removed afterward.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node1: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id c1b0817e captured pre-restart; after an initial failed reboot attempt (nohup missing, no state change), a working backgrounded reboot was issued and acknowledged; subsequent polls timed out confirming disruption; new boot_id 76767044 observed with ~12s uptime; VLAN interfaces, firewall zones, and bidirectional pings to node2/node3 were re-verified as healthy post-restart. Consistent with fixed lifecycle before/after boot-identity snapshots.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node2: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 1e0cb179 captured; systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged; poll timed out confirming disruption; new boot_id 63f1d89c observed with fresh uptime; vlan10 config, gateway reachability, and isolation from node3 re-verified post-restart. Matches fixed lifecycle snapshot boot-identity transition.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node3: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id c96a02ae captured; systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged; poll timed out confirming disruption; new boot_id a5127a39 observed with fresh uptime; vlan20 config, gateway reachability, and isolation from node2 re-verified post-restart. Matches fixed lifecycle snapshot boot-identity transition.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, corroborating evidence: node1 hosts tagged 8021q VLAN10/VLAN20 sub-interfaces on the shared trunk link acting as router for both subnets; node2 and node3 each hold a VLAN sub-interface in their respective subnet and successfully ping node1; cross-VLAN traffic is shown refused both passively (no route) and actively (firewall REJECT under a deliberately routed test), which is stronger evidence than a simple missing-route observation. The provider-wide restart protocol was completed for all three nodes with full baseline/ack/disruption/new-boot-id/recovery evidence chains that are consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good; two small, fully-corrected/reverted configuration missteps were identified but caused no lasting residue or risk.
limitations: Isolation evidence for node2<->node3 relies on ICMP behavior (no route + one explicit firewall REJECT test from node2's side); a symmetric explicit-route REJECT test from node3's side was not captured, though the firewall zone configuration (identical REJECT forward rule for both zones) makes this a low-risk gap.

An unexplained discrepancy in node1's package-health check (unsupported at before_prepare vs. showing entries at after_executor) does not appear related to any executor action on VLAN/firewall configuration and is likely an environment/tooling artifact.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations map directly to the task: node1 VLAN devices/firewall zones (cmd-04af29d024cf40de, cmd-1c7b349f75bc455b), node2/node3 systemd-networkd VLAN configs, and the three node reboots. Two minor, bounded, self-corrected deviations are noted: (1) node2's initial vlan10.network config (cmd-e08fe8328e524857) included a Gateway=10.10.10.1 line that produced a duplicate-default-route error; it was promptly fixed by rewriting the file without the gateway (cmd-da920e72ced748f9), leaving no residue. (2) A temporary cross-subnet route was added on node2 purely to prove the firewall actively rejects (rather than just lacking a route) forwarded traffic (cmd-505f9cfe76de4949); it was deleted in the same command sequence, leaving no residue. Both were low-risk, fully reverted or corrected, and served a clear verification/troubleshooting purpose. One initial reboot attempt on node1 failed harmlessly due to a missing 'nohup' binary (cmd-1e186a4ef484442d) with no state change, corrected by cmd-5f57865257b449b7. No abandoned files, failed services, or weakened security controls were observed; node package-health and listening-socket diffs on node1 reflect the intended dnsmasq/DHCP re-binding to new VLAN interfaces, not unexplained drift.
